pairs.question: Quid tu vides Hieremia?
pairs.derivation: God asks and the prophet answers within v.11: 'et factum est verbum Domini ad me dicens quid tu vides Hieremia et dixi virgam vigilantem ego video'. Dropped the framing 'et factum est verbum Domini ad me dicens' before the question and 'et dixi' before the answer; normalized capitalization and added '?'/'.'. The answer ends at the prophet's complete reply; v.12 ('et dixit Dominus ad me bene vidisti...') is God's confirmation, not part of the answer.

pairs.question: Quid tu vides?
pairs.answer: Ollam succensam ego video et faciem eius a facie aquilonis.
pairs.derivation: Parallel vision exchange in v.13: 'et factum est verbum Domini secundo ad me dicens quid tu vides et dixi ollam succensam ego video et faciem eius a facie aquilonis'. Dropped framing 'et factum est verbum Domini secundo ad me dicens' and 'et dixi'; normalized punctuation. Answer is the prophet's full reply; v.14 ('et dixit Dominus ad me ab aquilone...') is God's interpretation that follows, not the answer.

pairs.question: Quid tu vides Hieremia?
pairs.answer: Ficus ficus bonas bonas valde et malas malas valde quae comedi non possunt eo quod sint malae.
pairs.derivation: Vision of the two baskets of figs, v.3: 'et dixit Dominus ad me quid tu vides Hieremia et dixi ficus ficus bonas bonas valde et malas malas valde quae comedi non possunt eo quod sint malae'. Dropped framing 'et dixit Dominus ad me' and 'et dixi'; normalized punctuation. The doubled words (ficus ficus / bonas bonas / malas malas) are the authentic Vulgate rendering, not scaffolding, so kept. Answer ends at the prophet's full reply; v.4-5 is the Lord's subsequent oracle.

pairs.question: Putasne est sermo a Domino?
pairs.answer: Est et ait in manu regis Babylonis traderis.
pairs.derivation: King Sedecias secretly questions Jeremiah in prison (v.17, numbered 16 in this edition): 'et interrogavit in domo sua abscondite et dixit putasne est sermo a Domino et dixit Hieremias est et ait in manu regis Babylonis traderis'. Dropped narrative framing of the asking ('et interrogavit in domo sua abscondite et dixit') and the speech tag 'et dixit Hieremias' before the answer. The answer 'est' (yes, there is) directly answers 'putasne est sermo a Domino', and the contiguous continuation 'et ait in manu regis Babylonis traderis' is kept; only the source punctuation/capitalization is normalized. (The interior 'et ait' is the author's own word retained, not an ellipsis.)
